questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.stem: A beekeeper logbook notes a cell structure storing genetic material; which organelle is this?

options.text: The nucleus houses DNA and controls cell activities

The ribosome stores DNA and transcribes genes
The Golgi apparatus archives genetic information

questions.explanation: The nucleus contains DNA and regulates cell activities. The mitochondrion idea overstates its genetic role in this context.

options.text: Chloroplasts for photosynthesis

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.stem: A beekeeper logbook asks why cells stay small; what is the main reason?

DNA cannot fit in large cells

questions.explanation: As cells grow, volume increases faster than surface area, limiting exchange efficiency. The DNA idea is not the primary constraint.
questions.hint: Surface area must keep up with volume.

questions.explanation: Gene expression changes, not DNA sequence, drive specialization. A tempting wrong idea is that cells lose genes during differentiation.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.stem: A beekeeper logbook asks how cells detect external signals; what is the mechanism?

options.text: Lipids directly bind hormones and enter the nucleus
Receptor proteins bind signaling molecules and trigger responses
Carbohydrates on the membrane secrete signals outward
The nucleus extends through the membrane to sense signals

questions.explanation: Receptor proteins bind external signals and initiate cellular responses. Lipids do not specifically bind hormones.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.stem: A beekeeper logbook asks how plant cells communicate; which structure enables this?

options.text: Tight junctions connect plant cells
Gap junctions are the main plant cell connectors
Plasmodesmata connect adjacent plant cells
Plant cells do not communicate directly

questions.explanation: Plasmodesmata are channels connecting plant cells. Gap and tight junctions are animal cell structures.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.stem: A beekeeper logbook asks how one zygote produces trillions of diverse cells; explain.

answer.exemplar: The zygote divides repeatedly, and differential gene expression in daughter cells produces specialized structures and functions while DNA stays constant.

questions.explanation: Repeated division plus selective gene expression creates diversity from one genome. A tempting wrong idea is that DNA changes create diversity.
questions.hint: Division plus gene expression creates diversity.
